text:
maria (eng-infra): Heads up — retention job last night ballooned. We pushed ~12GB more spans than expected into cold storage for tenant: acme. Seen multiple exporter retries in the logs.
telemetry-bot: alert: exporter_retry_rate > 5% for service=inference-runtime in region=us-west-2
sam (eng-platform): ugh. any idea what changed? recent deploys to sdk or runtime?
maria (eng-infra): rough trace: simultaneous model swap for several tenants + SDK reinit on config reload. Exporter creation path does a full re-connect which causes temporary duplication and spike. snippet from logs: 
```
2026-02-28T03:12:01Z ERROR exporter: connect timeout, retrying (tenant=acme, conn=2)
2026-02-28T03:12:01Z WARN  exporter: queued spans=45321 memory=420MB
```
jia (eng-runtime): This aligns with the Rust side: we were reinitializing per-tenant exporter on config refresh. Reinit path currently creates new exporter then lets old one drain in background with unlimited concurrency. If many tenants flip at once we spawn dozens of drain tasks. Memory + duplicated fanout = spike.
oliver (eng-ml): From model/metrics side, we see duplicated kv-cache spans (same request repeated) — the fanout to per-tenant exporters was the amplification. We should avoid per-tenant full rebinds if possible.
dani (eng-sre): Prior incidents show long drains can also hold on to large KV cache references. We need bounded concurrency and backpressure on span ingestion.
sam (eng-platform): Agreed. Proposal: introduce an exporter-rotation API that atomically swaps exporter refs and returns a drain future. Rotation should: 1) make new exporter start accepting, 2) stop routing new spans to old exporter, 3) wait up to X seconds for in-flight spans, then force-flush or drop.
maria (eng-infra): +1. Also add a global semaphore per-process limiting concurrent drains (default 4). If semaphore exhausted, rotation should queue or reject config change.
jia (eng-runtime): Implementation sketch for the SDK surface (single-string, pseudo):
```
# python
class TelemetryClient:
    def rotate_exporter(self, new_exporter, timeout_ms=5000) -> Future[str]:
        """Atomically swap exporters. Returns 'drained'|'timed_out'|'forced'"""
```
```
// go
func (c *TelemetryClient) SwapExporter(ctx context.Context, new Exporter, timeout time.Duration) (Result, error)
```
```rust
impl TelemetryClient {
    fn swap_exporter(&self, new: Arc<dyn Exporter>, timeout: Duration) -> DrainOutcome {}
}
```
sam (eng-platform): Important: keep API small and same semantics across Python/Go/Rust. Consumers expect a short blocking or a future they can await in deploy hooks.

oliver (eng-ml): We should also change routing: route-by-tenant pointer to exporter ref (opaque pointer) rather than copying routing lists. Swap pointer once — no per-span branch to decide old/new. That reduces per-span cost.
dani (eng-sre): On drain behavior: prefer force-flush to remote when timeout happens, then fallback to disk buffer with bounded size and eviction oldest-first. Disk spool should be a last resort for tenants with retention toggled on.
maria (eng-infra): Sampling and attribute sanitization also contributed: we were logging full prompt for some spans (attr blowup). Add char-limit on string attrs (e.g. 1024) and truncate plus a hash for dedupe.
jia (eng-runtime): For Rust/Go it's cheap to add attr truncation at collector boundary. Python needs careful GC patterns to avoid retention through closures.
sam (eng-platform): UX changes for console: show "Exporter rotation status" per-tenant in rollout UI with states: pending, draining, timed_out, forced_flushed. Expose drain duration and memory delta.
oliver (eng-ml): Also surface sampling rate used for rollouts so teams can correlate missing spans.
dani (eng-sre): Action items:
- implement rotation API in Python/Go/Rust SDKs (jia + sam)
- add process-wide drain semaphore + queueing (maria)
- attr truncation at boundary (oliver)
- disk spool design doc + size limits (dani)
- console status + metrics (sam)

maria (eng-infra): I can start a short doc with diagrams. Will include a fallback timeline (connect -> swap -> drain 0..T -> force_flush -> spool).
sam (eng-platform): I'll draft API ergonomics and a small compatibility shim for older SDKs.
jia (eng-runtime): I'll prototype swap in Rust this week and run a chaos test flipping 200 tenants. Will post perf numbers.
dani (eng-sre): Please include failure scenarios: exporter rejects, partial handshake, and how we'll signal to SRE.
telemetry-bot: created incident ticket INF-2026-042: exporter-rotation-memory-spike
maria (eng-infra): tagging followups: @sam (eng-platform) @jia (eng-runtime) @dani (eng-sre) — let's sync tomorrow 10am PT. If anyone can't make it ping here. :calendar: :thumbsup:
